p: Edinburgh Zoo's address on Corstorphine Road puts it right on one of the main routes in from the west, with frequent buses from the city centre stopping outside, so leaving the car behind is easy. If you are driving, the road can be busy at peak times, so give yourself some leeway. Once inside, start at the bottom and work your way up, saving energy for the climb, and you'll be rewarded with views over the city and the hills beyond.

Worth knowing before you go: the zoo's giant pandas, Tian Tian and Yang Guang, returned to China at the end of 2023, so you won't find them here now. There's still plenty to enjoy, from the koalas to the penguins and a whole hillside of other residents to meet.

Corstorphine Hill itself is a local nature reserve, with woodland paths leading up behind the zoo, a walled garden and Clermiston Tower, built to mark the centenary of Sir Walter Scott's birth. On the way into the city, you'll pass close to Murrayfield, Scotland's national rugby stadium. Further in, the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, a free-to-enter garden in Inverleith, has glasshouses, rock gardens and sweeping views of the skyline. The National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street is free and packed with treasures, including Dolly the sheep, while Dynamic Earth, beneath Arthur's Seat, takes you on a journey through the history of the planet. With so much on offer, the zoo is just the start of a fantastic trip to the capital.
